verses.text: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
He makes me lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside quiet waters.
He restores my soul; He guides me in the paths of righteousness for the sake of His name.
Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me; Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me.
You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows.
Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever.

context.author: The title says “of David” (Hebrew le-David), which can mean by David, for David or about David. Seventy-three psalms carry his name; tradition and the New Testament take many of them as his.
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship in Jerusalem, and every reader who prays
context.setting: David, once a shepherd boy at Bethlehem (1 Samuel 16:11), writes, “The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want” (v.1). The Shepherd makes him lie down in green pastures, leads him beside quiet waters and restores his soul (vv.2-3). “Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me; Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me” (v.4). Then the picture changes to a host: “You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows” (v.5). “Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever” (v.6).
context.custom: Eastern shepherds walked ahead of their flocks and called them by name (John 10:3-4). The rod was a club for driving off wild animals (1 Samuel 17:34-35); the staff, a long crook, guided and lifted the sheep. In dry country the shepherd had to find water still enough for sheep to drink. A host who welcomed a guest protected him from enemies, anointed his head with oil and kept his cup full.
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 24 asks who may ascend the hill of the LORD, and welcomes the King of Glory.
context.timelineBible: Jesus said, “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down His life for the sheep” (John 10:11). Ezekiel 34 condemns Israel’s selfish shepherds and promises that God Himself will shepherd His flock. Revelation says, “the Lamb in the center of the throne will be their shepherd” (Revelation 7:17).

translation.meaning: To pasture, tend, shepherd. Kings were called shepherds of their people (2 Samuel 5:2).
A staff to lean on, a support.
To pursue, chase. God’s goodness and mercy chase after David.

gospelParallels.note: You have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.

otBackground.note: I Myself will search for My sheep.
He tends His flock like a shepherd.
David the shepherd fights the lion and the bear.

overview.summary: David trusts the LORD as his shepherd who provides, guides and stays with him through the darkest valley, and as his host who welcomes him forever.
overview.settingLine: Pastures and valleys in the Judean hills.

history.t: He kept his father’s sheep at Bethlehem.

customs.t: Oil on the head for honor and refreshment.

archaeology.t: Stone pens in the Judean hills sheltered flocks at night.
Hammurabi called himself the shepherd of his people.

overview.discussion: “You are with me” (v.4). Where is my valley right now, and what would it change to know the Shepherd is with me in it?
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (1-20 in the app so far). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
overview.author: David
